craft_notes: Sthāyin: the supremacy claim. Sanskrit-first: yady-api anyaprasaṅgeṣu kept concessive frame; samyak kept (true — the intensifier is the claim); dāyikā kept giver (active). Rows: 9 (other-connections/Gītā pair), 1 ('gives true attainment' closes — dāyikā end-weight). Close: 'gives true attainment.' Rejected: 'merely celebrated' — kept celebrated (gīyate passive, no mereness added); softening samyak — killed: it's the superlative.

lines: Other connections celebrate liberation by name;
yet this Bhagavadgītā gives true attainment.
l4.sanskrit_cite: yadyapyanyaprasaṅgeṣu mokṣo nāmātra gīyate tathāpi bhagavadgītāḥ samyaktatprāptidāyikāḥ

reads_against.argmap: How does the Gītā compare to other mokṣa-celebrations? → Other texts sing mokṣa incidentally; the Gītā gives samyak-prāpti — the supremacy claim is exclusive (samyak retained).
c1_essence: Other texts sing mokṣa incidentally; the Bhagavadgītā gives true attainment.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta-śānta of the treasury opened (wonder at the work's own store)
